{"author":{"id":"U_kgDOBch6VA","is_bot":false,"login":"stlindenau","name":""},"body":"### What happened?

`entire session resume` restores the transcript to a hardcoded `~/.claude/projects/...` and ignores the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable that Claude Code itself honours.

On any setup that relocates the Claude config directory, the restored transcript lands somewhere the agent will not look — so `claude -r <id>` cannot find it. Worse, in my case it lands on storage the user has deliberately moved *away* from.

`entire session resume --help` exposes no flag to redirect the destination. The string `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` does appear in the binary, so it seems to be understood elsewhere in the codebase, just not on the restore path.

I hit this while evaluating Entire for moving agent sessions between two machines. Everything else in that flow worked well — see "Additional context" below, because I think the surrounding design is right and this is a one-line-ish gap in it.

### Steps to reproduce

Two clones of the same repo, each with its own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, and a bare repo standing in for the remote.

**machineA** — capture and push a session:

```bash
export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/configA
entire enable --telemetry=false --agent claude-code --yes
claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits "Edit app.py so it prints 'hello world'. Then reply DONE."
git commit -am "feat: print hello world"     # checkpoint created, Entire-Checkpoint trailer added
git push origin main
# [entire] Pushing 1 checkpoint ref(s) to origin... done
```

**machineB** — a second clone, different config dir:

```bash
export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/configB
git fetch origin '+refs/entire/*:refs/entire/*'
entire session resume main
```

**Expected** — the transcript is written under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`:

```
/tmp/configB/projects/<encoded-cwd>/d3d706a8-9061-48df-bddc-f5080ae5c1d5.jsonl
```

**Actual** — it is written under the hardcoded default, and `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` stays empty:

```console
$ entire session resume main
Writing transcript to: /home/vscode/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/d3d706a8-9061-48df-bddc-f5080ae5c1d5.jsonl
✓ Restored session d3d706a8-9061-48df-bddc-f5080ae5c1d5.

$ find "$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR" -name '*.jsonl' | wc -l
0
```

### Entire CLI version

Entire CLI 0.10.6 (Go 1.26.6, linux/amd64)

### OS and architecture

Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 (Ubuntu, inside a dev container on WSL2)

### Agent

Claude Code 2.1.220

### Terminal

VS Code integrated terminal (bash)

### Suggested fix

On the restore path, resolve the config root as `os.Getenv("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR")` falling back to `~/.claude`, matching Claude Code's own precedence. A `--config-dir` flag on `session resume` would also work, though honouring the environment variable is the smaller surprise.

Happy to test a patch against the reproduction above.

### Additional context

**Why this matters beyond preference.** We point `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` at a mounted volume specifically so transcripts survive a container rebuild. A restore that writes to the container-local default gets destroyed by the next rebuild — and because the restore reports success, the loss is silent until someone goes looking for the conversation.

The other case is several isolated config directories on one machine: restoring into the shared default merges state that was deliberately kept apart.

**The rest of the flow is genuinely good**, which is why this stands out. Rewriting the project directory for the destination's own path is exactly the right call — it is what let a *pinned, older* Claude Code (2.1.220, which cannot do cross-directory `--resume`) resolve a session that arrived from a different checkout. I moved a session between two clones through a git ref and resumed it with full context intact; asked what it had edited, it described the change correctly and even noticed the file belonged to the other checkout. This one path is the only thing stopping that from working with a relocated config directory.

Also worth noting: a plain `git clone` does not fetch `refs/entire/*` (default refspec is `refs/heads/*`), so the explicit refspec above is needed. That may be obvious to you, but it was not to me from the README.

input.content:
# Fix #2367: `session resume` ignores `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`

## Context

`entire session resume` restores a transcript to `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<id>.jsonl` even when the user has relocated Claude Code's config directory with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. Claude Code then cannot find the restored session, and on setups that moved the config dir to survive container rebuilds the restore lands on storage that is wiped next rebuild, with a success message.

Claude Code's docs state that when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set, **every** `~/.claude` path lives under it instead. Entire models that correctly in exactly one place today (the `settings.json` lookup used to re-inject `apiKeyHelper`) and ignores it in the three that matter for sessions and skills. There is no shared cross-agent helper; Codex (`resolveCodexHome`) and pi (`resolvePiHome`) each have a per-package resolver with the same shape, and Copilot honors `COPILOT_HOME` inline. Claude Code is the one agent with no resolver.

**Outcome:** one unexported resolver in the `claudecode` package answers "where is Claude's config dir" for every caller, so the four sites that join `.claude` onto the home dir stop knowing about the env var.

## Root cause

`cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/claude.go:95-119` — `GetSessionDir` and `GetSessionBaseDir` do `os.UserHomeDir()` + `.claude/projects`. Everything on the restore path derives the destination from `GetSessionDir(repoRoot)`: `resume.go:923` (the pre-create `MkdirAll`), `strategy/manual_commit_pending.go:406` (`RestoreLogsOnly`), and `agent/session_store.go:58` (`sessionStoreForWrite` anchors the write root on it). So fixing `GetSessionDir` fixes the command with no changes to the strategy or store.

Sites that join `.claude` onto the home dir (all in `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/`):

| site | today | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `claude.go:95` `GetSessionDir` | `~/.claude/projects/<enc>` | `<cfg>/projects/<enc>` |
| `claude.go:113` `GetSessionBaseDir` | `~/.claude/projects` | `<cfg>/projects` |
| `generate.go:114` `userClaudeSettingsPath` | already honors env, own copy | `<cfg>/settings.json` via resolver |
| `discovery.go:34-52` `DiscoverReviewSkills` | `~/.claude/{plugins/cache,skills,commands,agents}` | same under `<cfg>` |

Beyond resume, this also repairs `attach`'s cross-project fallback walk (`transcript.go:64`), agent auto-detection from a hook's transcript path (`agent.AgentForTranscriptPath`, used by `resolveSessionAgentType` and `shouldSkipForwardedHook`), and review-skill discovery for anyone with a relocated config dir.

## Design

In `claude.go`, next to `GetSessionDir` (mirrors `resolveCodexHome` / `resolvePiHome` placement):

```go
// claudeConfigDirEnvVar relocates Claude Code's configuration directory
// (~/.claude by default). Claude Code documents that every ~/.claude path lives
// under it when set, so transcripts, settings, skills and plugins move together.
const claudeConfigDirEnvVar = "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR"

// resolveClaudeConfigDir returns Claude Code's configuration directory:
// $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR when set, else ~/.claude.
func resolveClaudeConfigDir() (string, error) {
	if dir := os.Getenv(claudeConfigDirEnvVar); dir != "" {
		if err := userdirs.RequireAbsoluteOverride(claudeConfigDirEnvVar, dir); err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		return dir, nil
	}
	home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get home directory: %w", err)
	}
	return filepath.Join(home, ".claude"), nil
}
```

Resolution order in `GetSessionDir` stays: `ENTIRE_TEST_CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` (test override, no encoding) → `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (encoding still applies) → `~/.claude`. Same order pi documents at `pi.go:130-131`.

**One judgment call: a relative `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is refused, not resolved.** Reuses the single house implementation `userdirs.RequireAbsoluteOverride` (`internal/entireclient/userdirs/userdirs.go:60`). Rationale is the one CLAUDE.md gives for Entire's own overrides: a relative value resolves against the working directory, which is the repo root inside a hook but wherever the user is for `session resume`, so the same environment would scatter transcripts across directories. Claude Code's handling of a relative value is undocumented, so matching it is not an option; refusing with a message naming the variable is the only choice that cannot be wrong. Cost: three lines and one test. Callers that are best-effort (`readUserAPIKeyHelper`, `DiscoverReviewSkills`) already swallow the error; `resume`/`attach` surface it. Strike this if you prefer pass-through like `CODEX_HOME`.

Dropped on purpose: the `strings.TrimSpace` that `userClaudeSettingsPath` applied today. Nothing else trims an agent's home var, and a whitespace-padded value is now refused as relative rather than silently rewritten.

No new flag. The reporter's own read is that honoring the env var is the smaller surprise, and a `--config-dir` flag would be a second way to say the same thing.

## Steps (TDD order)

### 1. Reproducing integration test (fails first)

`cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/resume_test.go` — add `TestResume_HonorsClaudeConfigDir`, shaped like `TestResume_SwitchBranchWithSession` (lines 30-92): create a session, commit with shadow hooks, switch to master, then run resume with a hand-built env instead of `env.RunResume`:

```go
cfgDir := t.TempDir()
cmd := execx.NonInteractive(ctx, getTestBinary(), "session", "resume", featureBranch)
cmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
cmd.Env = append(testutil.GitIsolatedEnv(),
	"ENTIRE_TEST_CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=", // empty: exercise the real resolution
	"CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="+cfgDir,
)
```

Assert exactly one match for `filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(cfgDir, "projects", "*", session.ID+".jsonl"))` (glob the encoded segment rather than recomputing it, as line 85 does) and that the output names `cfgDir` in its `Writing transcript to:` line. This is the reporter's scenario and is red today.

### 2. Unit tests in `claudecode` (fail first)

`claude_test.go` (already `package claudecode`, already has the two `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` settings tests at lines 200-217; add beside them, all `t.Setenv`, so no `t.Parallel`):

- `TestResolveClaudeConfigDir` table: env set to absolute → that value; env empty → `filepath.Join(home, ".claude")` where `home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()` (platform-agnostic, no HOME faking); env relative (`"relative/cfg"`) → error whose text contains `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.
- `TestGetSessionDir_HonorsClaudeConfigDir`: `t.Setenv("ENTIRE_TEST_CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR", "")`, `t.Setenv("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR", cfg)`; want `filepath.Join(cfg, "projects", SanitizePathForClaude("/Users/foo/repo"))`. Mirrors `pi/session_resolve_test.go:50-63` and `copilotcli_test.go:127-140`.
- `TestGetSessionBaseDir_HonorsClaudeConfigDir`: want `filepath.Join(cfg, "projects")`.

`discovery_test.go` (`package claudecode_test`):

- `withFakeHome` gains `t.Setenv("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR", "") // hermetic: a dev shell's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR must not leak in` — identical to `codex/discovery_test.go:22`.
- `TestDiscoverReviewSkills_HonorsClaudeConfigDir`: `withFakeHome(t)`, `cfg := t.TempDir()`, `t.Setenv("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR", cfg)`, write `cfg/skills/code-review/SKILL.md`, assert it is discovered. Mirrors `TestCodexAgent_DiscoverReviewSkills_HonorsCodexHome` at `codex/discovery_test.go:116-132`.

### 3. Implementation

## Context

Claude Code's docs state that when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set, **every** `~/.claude` path lives under it instead. Entire models that correctly in exactly one place today (the `settings.json` lookup used to re-inject `apiKeyHelper`) and ignores it in the three that matter for sessions and skills. There is no shared cross-agent helper; Codex (`resolveCodexHome`) and pi (`resolvePiHome`) each have a per-package resolver with the same shape, and Copilot honors `COPILOT_HOME` inline. Claude Code is the one agent with no resolver.

Fix for #2367 is implemented and verified on `fix-hardcoded-claude-home`, uncommitted. Ten files changed.

**Root cause.** Claude Code's `GetSessionDir` and `GetSessionBaseDir` hardcoded `~/.claude/projects`. Every restore path derives its destination from `GetSessionDir`, so the whole fix sits in the `claudecode` package. Nothing in the strategy or session store changed.

**What changed**

- **One resolver**, `resolveClaudeConfigDir` in `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/claude.go`, returns `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set and `~/.claude` otherwise. Claude Code's docs state every `~/.claude` path moves under that variable, so the swap is wholesale.
- **Four consumers** now go through it: session dir, session base dir, the `settings.json` lookup that already honored the variable with its own copy, and review-skill discovery. Beyond resume, this also repairs attach's cross-project fallback and agent auto-detection from a hook's transcript path.
- **A relative value is refused** via the existing `userdirs.RequireAbsoluteOverride`, with the house `nolint:wrapcheck` comment. This is the one judgment call in the plan. Reason: a relative path resolves against cwd, which is the repo root in a hook but arbitrary for `session resume`, so one environment would scatter transcripts. Claude's own relative handling is undocumented.
- **Tests**: an integration test reproducing the issue's exact scenario (red before, green after), a resolver table test, and one honors-test each for session dir, base dir, and discovery.
- **Hermetic harnesses**: the `cli` and integration TestMains now unset `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, and the discovery test helper clears it. Without this, a developer's relocated config dir would outrank the `HOME` steer in the attach fallback tests. Verified by running that test with a bogus value exported.
- **Docs**: the review-command discovery roots and the agent-guide `GetSessionDir` row now mention the relocation variables.

**Verification**

- `mise run test`, `mise run test:integration`, `mise run test:e2e:canary`: all pass.
- `mise run fmt && mise run lint`: clean. Lint works locally again; I updated the stale memory note that said it was broken.
- Command-level check on a built binary: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=rel/cfg entire session attach ...` fails with a message naming the variable and value.

**Not done**

- No commit, since you did not ask for one. The tree is ready for `git commit`.
- The two-machine repro with a real `claude` binary was not run. Real-agent E2E costs tokens and the repo rules forbid running it proactively. The integration test covers the same flow with simulated hooks.
- My first red run wrote one test transcript into my real `~/.claude/projects`, which is the bug itself in action. I removed that directory afterward.

geminicli: honor GEMINI_CLI_HOME when resolving Gemini's session dirs

Gemini CLI resolves ~ through its own homedir() helper, which returns
GEMINI_CLI_HOME when set, and every storage path, chats included, appends
.gemini underneath it. Entire resolved the session dir and base dir from
the real home only, so `entire session resume` restored transcripts to
~/.gemini while Gemini looked under $GEMINI_CLI_HOME/.gemini, and attach's
cross-project fallback walked the wrong tree.

One resolver now answers which home Gemini uses, and both session-dir
methods go through it. The variable replaces the home directory, not
~/.gemini, so .gemini is still appended, unlike CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. A
relative override is refused rather than resolved against a per-process
working directory. Test harnesses unset GEMINI_CLI_HOME alongside
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR so a developer's relocated home cannot outrank the HOME
steer the attach fallback tests rely on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
